content_list.content_text: For nearly a century, a film's fate was decided by a predictable chain: the studio bought ads, critics published their reviews and, finally, audiences voted with their tickets. In the 2020s, that order got scrambled. With theaters shut by the pandemic and the phone turned into the main screen of the day, the conversation about movies migrated to TikTok, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram and Letterboxd. There, viewers stopped being mere targets of marketing and became its co-authors: they invent nicknames, turn scenes into dance trends, create events no executive ever planned and, when they feel like it, bury a release with irony. This chapter tells how memes turned into box office (and sometimes didn't), how studios learned to speak the language of social media and how a new generation of cinephiles began logging, rating and rediscovering films in public.

information.contentText: Two days before the July 21, 2023 release, a theater marquee was already advertising the double feature with the hashtag coined by internet users.

content_list.content_text: The most famous case was born of a scheduling accident. In October 2021, Universal set July 21, 2023, as the release date for Oppenheimer (2023), Christopher Nolan's drama about the father of the atomic bomb. In April 2022, Warner Bros. put Barbie (2023), Greta Gerwig's pink comedy starring Margot Robbie, on the same date. By the old logic, it would have been a release-date war, and one of the two films would come out wounded. The internet decided otherwise. The contrast between the doll and the bomb became a joke, the joke got a name, Barbenheimer, and the name became a plan: see both films on the same day, ideally dressed for the occasion. On opening weekend, the two grossed about US$ 244 million combined in the United States and accounted for nearly eight out of every ten tickets sold that weekend. The biggest movie event of the decade was not invented by any marketing department.

information.contentText: The official trailer for Barbie, whose pink aesthetic became raw material for thousands of memes, mashups and costumes. On the other side of Barbenheimer, the gravity of Oppenheimer completed the joke.

content_list.content_text: The meme, however, is not a ticket-selling machine. Morbius (2022), from Sony, with Jared Leto as the Marvel vampire, opened in April 2022, was savaged by critics (a 15% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes) and made US$ 167.5 million worldwide, a flop. Online, however, it got a second life: users pretended it was the greatest masterpiece in history, made up box-office grosses of “one morbillion dollars” and spread the line “It's Morbin' time,” which is never said in the film, a pun on the Power Rangers battle cry. Sony took the joke seriously and re-released the film in more than a thousand theaters on June 3, 2022. The weekend brought in about US$ 310,000, less than US$ 300 per theater. The irony generated likes, not tickets: nobody wanted to pay to see something that was only funny as a joke.

content_list.title: Barbenheimer: how the internet created an event
content_list.description: The word Barbenheimer first appeared in a tweet on April 15, 2022, posted by Matt Neglia, editor of the website Next Best Picture, who later said he didn't even remember writing it. In little more than a year, the term spawned T-shirts, fake posters fusing pink and flames, guides to the right order for the double feature and a dress code: pink for one film, black for the other. The AMC chain reported that more than 20,000 members of its loyalty program had bought advance tickets to see both films on the same day; on the eve of the release, the number had reached 40,000. Tom Cruise joined in by posting a photo with tickets for both, and Gerwig and Robbie responded with tickets for Oppenheimer and the new Mission: Impossible. In the end, Barbie reached US$ 1.44 billion worldwide, Oppenheimer came close to US$ 1 billion, and the two earned a combined 21 nominations at the 2024 Oscars and eight statuettes — seven of them for Oppenheimer, including Best Picture. The lesson for Hollywood was clear and a little uncomfortable: a connected audience can turn a scheduling coincidence into a collective ritual, something no amount of money can guarantee.

content_list.content_text: A month later, another meme showed the opposite path. When Minions: The Rise of Gru (2022) opened in July 2022, groups of teenagers began showing up to screenings in suits, imitating the villain Gru. The prank, which reportedly started with Australian students, spread across TikTok under the hashtag #Gentleminions: young men in ties filing into the theater, applauding, making the character's steepled-fingers gesture and sometimes throwing bananas at the screen. Some British theaters went as far as banning suited groups because of the rowdiness, while the franchise itself joined in on social media. The film opened with US$ 107 million in the United States over three days, and exit polls indicated that 34% of the audience was between 13 and 17, an unusual share for an animated film. The difference from Morbius is that the affection for the Minions, tied to that generation's childhood, was sincere, and the joke could only be completed inside the theater.

quote.quote: It's all love: double feature, and then double feature again.
quote.author: Greta Gerwig (at the Barbie premiere in Los Angeles, 2023)

content_list.content_text: That idea, the meme that needs the theater to happen, came back again and again. In April 2025, screenings of A Minecraft Movie (2025) turned into parties as teenagers began shouting “chicken jockey!” along with Jack Black, tossing popcorn in the air and filming the scene for TikTok. In August of the same year, KPop Demon Hunters (2025), a Netflix animated film, got special sing-along screenings, and they took the film to the top of the American box office for a weekend. These experiences recall the screenings of The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) that began in the 1970s: the film becomes a pretext for a collective ritual, and the video of the ritual becomes free advertising. For the studios, the lesson was twofold. Sincere engagement, which invites people to take part, fills theaters; mockery, which comments from the outside, merely goes viral.

The studios, of course, tried to manufacture their own viral moments. To launch Smile (2022), a horror film by Parker Finn, Paramount took the scares far away from theaters. On the weekend before the release, the marketing team bought seats behind home plate, right in the line of the TV cameras, at Major League Baseball games. There, actors spent minutes staring into the broadcast with fixed, creepy smiles, and clips of those moments spread across social media. The film, which cost US$ 17 million, opened with US$ 22.6 million. Months later, Universal insisted on putting in the trailer for M3GAN (2023), by Gerard Johnstone, the scene in which the killer doll dances before attacking. The choreography became a craze on TikTok, the campaign sent dancers dressed as M3GAN onto red carpets, and the film, which cost US$ 12 million, opened with US$ 30.4 million.

information.contentText: The trailer that showed off the doll's dance and helped turn a modestly budgeted horror film into what the American press called “the first blockbuster of TikTok.”

content_list.content_text: Social media also began choosing what gets made into a movie. On BookTok, the community of readers on TikTok, videos of people sobbing as they finished a book became a powerful showcase. The most lucrative case was Colleen Hoover's: her novel It Ends with Us, published in 2016, exploded on the app in 2021, reached the top of the New York Times best-seller list in January 2022 and was the best-selling novel in the United States in 2022 and again in 2023. The adaptation, It Ends with Us (2024), starring Blake Lively, opened to about US$ 50 million and topped US$ 350 million worldwide; according to exit polls, 30% of the audience went because of the book. The same network that created the audience also passed judgment on the campaign: the flower-filled promotion, with invitations to go “with the girls,” was harshly criticized for softening a novel about domestic violence.

quote.quote: Going viral is something you can prepare for, but it's not something you can actually create.
quote.author: Michael Moses (Universal's chief marketing officer, on M3GAN, 2023)

content_list.content_text: Sometimes the internet resurrects a film and, as a bonus, a song. Saltburn (2023), by Emerald Fennell, had a quiet theatrical run at the end of 2023, grossing about US$ 21 million worldwide. When it arrived on Prime Video on December 22, it became the movie everyone was talking about: its most daring scenes, led by Barry Keoghan, inspired reaction videos and parodies, and clips about the film racked up nearly 4 billion views on TikTok. The final dance, set to “Murder on the Dancefloor,” Sophie Ellis-Bextor's 2001 hit, sent the song back up the charts: in January 2024 it again reached No. 2 in the United Kingdom, the same position it had hit 22 years earlier, and entered the American Billboard Hot 100 for the first time.

information.contentText: The fixed grin that haunts Smile left the screen and landed in the stands: actors hired by Paramount smiled into the TV cameras during baseball games, in one of the most talked-about marketing stunts of 2022.

content_list.content_text: If TikTok is the stage for virality, Letterboxd became the young cinephile's living room. Launched in New Zealand in 2011, the social network works like a diary: each user logs the films they have seen, rates them from half a star to five stars, writes reviews and builds lists. In 2020, it had about 1.8 million members. It grew during the pandemic and never stopped: it reached 10 million in 2023 and passed 30 million in June 2026. In 2023, according to the company itself, half of its active users were under 35. Its short, snarky reviews circulate as screenshots on X and TikTok, each profile's “four favorites” became a must-ask question in press-tour interviews, and Martin Scorsese, after joining the platform in October 2023, quickly became its most-followed member. The Academy, which hands out the Oscars, had already partnered with the site in early 2023.

information.contentText: Trailer for Saltburn, by Emerald Fennell. Low-key in theaters, the film became a phenomenon once it hit streaming and social media turned its most daring scenes into memes.

content_list.content_text: The power of social media also has a dark side. The #ReleaseTheSnyderCut campaign, which for years pressed Warner to release Zack Snyder's version of Justice League, combined petitions, billboards and fundraising, and it won: announced in May 2020, Zack Snyder's Justice League (2021) premiered on HBO Max in March 2021, running four hours. But the movement was marred by attacks on critics, and in 2022 Rolling Stone reported that studio investigations had found fake accounts inflating the campaign. Review bombing, the flood of negative ratings from people who often haven't even seen the film, led Rotten Tomatoes to stop accepting audience scores before release and to prioritize verified ratings from ticket buyers. In 2025, IMDb posted an “unusual voting activity” notice on the page for Snow White (2025).

content_list.title: Letterboxd, the cinephile's diary
content_list.description: One surprise about Letterboxd is that its young users don't live on new releases alone: films from the current year usually account for less than a quarter of all logs. The rest is the past, and the platform's ranking of top-rated films has become a kind of canon chosen by the public. In mid-2026, the top spot among narrative features belonged to Harakiri (1962), Masaki Kobayashi's black-and-white samurai drama; before it, the No. 1 position had been held by The Godfather, Parasite, Everything Everywhere All at Once, the Soviet Come and See and Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse. In Los Angeles, the American Cinematheque tripled its membership compared with the pre-pandemic period and saw Hitchcock and Kurosawa screenings packed with audiences whose average age was around 27, an effect its programmers partly credit to Letterboxd. In December 2025, the platform took another step and launched the Letterboxd Video Store, a digital rental service for rare films or titles without a distributor. In July 2026, with a controlling stake in the company up for sale, reports named Netflix, Sony and Paramount among the interested parties, still in early talks: the cinephiles' diary had become a coveted asset.

content_list.content_text: In the end, the generation that grew up with a phone in hand did not abandon the movie theater; it started using it differently. A survey by Cinema United, the main trade association of U.S. exhibitors, found that Gen Z went to the movies an average of 6.1 times in 2025, up from 4.9 the year before, and that 41% of these young people went six times or more. To reach this audience, trailers got vertical versions and cuts just a few seconds long designed for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, and in 2026 Netflix launched a feed of vertical clips in its app. As early as 2020, Damien Chazelle had shot the short The Stunt Double for Apple on an iPhone: a journey through film history entirely in vertical format. The small screen stopped being just a showcase: in the chapter on internet creators, we will see filmmakers born there making their way to the big screen.

information.contentText: The HBO Max announcement used the fans' own hashtag as its title, acknowledging that Zack Snyder's version only existed because of a social media campaign.

movies.title: Barbie
movies.overview: No mundo mágico das Barbies, "Barbieland", uma das bonecas começa a perceber que não se encaixa como as outras. Depois de ser expulsa, ela parte para uma aventura no "mundo real", onde descobre que a beleza está no interior de cada um.

movies.title: Oppenheimer
movies.overview: A história do físico americano J. Robert Oppenheimer, seu papel no Projeto Manhattan e no desenvolvimento da bomba atômica durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial, e o quanto isso mudaria a história do mundo para sempre.

movies.title: Morbius
movies.overview: Gravemente doente com um raro distúrbio sanguíneo e determinado a salvar outros sofrendo o mesmo destino, o Dr. Morbius tenta uma aposta desesperada. O que primeiramente parece ser um sucesso radical, libera uma escuridão dentro dele e transforma esse médico em um caçador.

movies.title: Minions 2: A Origem de Gru
movies.overview: A continuação das aventuras dos Minions, sempre em busca de um líder tirânico. Dessa vez, eles ajudam um Gru ainda criança, descobrindo como ser vilão.

movies.title: Um Filme Minecraft
movies.overview: Quatro desajustados são subitamente puxados por um portal misterioso ao Mundo Superior: um paraíso bizarro e cúbico que vive na base da imaginação. Para voltar para casa, eles embarcam em uma jornada mágica com um artesão experiente e inusitado, Steve. Juntos, sua aventura desafiará todos os cinco a serem ousados e se reconectarem com as qualidades que tornam cada um deles singularmente criativo.

movies.title: Guerreiras do K-Pop
movies.overview: Quando não estão lotando estádios, as estrelas do K-pop Rumi, Mira e Zoey usam seus poderes secretos para proteger os fãs contra ameaças sobrenaturais.

movies.title: Sorria
movies.overview: Após testemunhar um acidente traumático e bizarro envolvendo um paciente, a Dra. Rose Cotter começa a vivenciar eventos assustadores que ela não consegue explicar.

movies.title: M3GAN
movies.overview: Uma brilhante roboticista de uma empresa de brinquedos usa inteligência artificial para desenvolver M3GAN, uma boneca realista programada para se relacionar emocionalmente com sua sobrinha recém-órfã. Mas quando a programação da boneca funciona muito bem, ela se torna superprotetora de sua nova amiga... com resultados aterrorizantes.

movies.title: É Assim Que Acaba
movies.overview: Lily Bloom, uma mulher que supera uma infância traumática para começar uma nova vida em Boston e perseguir o sonho de sua vida de abrir seu próprio negócio. Um encontro casual com o charmoso neurocirurgião Ryle Kincaid desencadeia uma conexão intensa, mas à medida que os dois se apaixonam profundamente, Lily começa a ver lados de Ryle que a lembram do relacionamento de seus pais. Quando o primeiro amor de Lily, Atlas Corrigan, reaparece repentinamente em sua vida, seu relacionamento com Ryle é abalado, e Lily percebe que deve aprender a confiar em sua própria força para fazer uma escolha impossível para o seu futuro.

movies.title: Saltburn
movies.overview: Uma história perversa sobre privilégio e desejo. Lutando para encontrar seu lugar na Faculdade de Oxford, o aluno Oliver Quick é atraído para o mundo do encantador e aristocrata Felix Catton, que o convida para Saltburn, a enorme mansão de sua família excêntrica, para passar um verão inesquecível.

movies.title: Liga da Justiça de Zack Snyder
movies.overview: Determinado a garantir que o sacrifício final do Superman não foi em vão, Bruce Wayne alinha forças com Diana Prince com planos de recrutar uma equipe de metahumanos para proteger o mundo de uma ameaça de proporções catastróficas que se aproxima.

movies.title: Harakiri
movies.overview: No século 18, o Japão não está mais em guerra e o país é governado com firmeza. Hanshiro Tsugumo, um dos muitos ronin (samurais errantes) desempregados, decide bater à porta do poderoso clã Ii. Recebido por Kageyu Saito, o intendente do clã, ele pede permissão para cometer suicídio por harakiri na residência. Tentando dissuadi-lo, Saito começa a lhe contar a história de Motome Chijiwa, outro ronin que também queria realizar o mesmo ritual no local.

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 2020 to Today
